chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, loves the spilling of blood and the feeding of food.

key_terms.إِهْرَاقَ الدِّمَاءِ: Spilling of blood (referring to sacrificial animals)

ai.seo_question: What does Allah love regarding blood and food according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the apparent paradox of 'spilling blood' is clarified by Shia scholars as referring specifically to the ritual slaughter of sacrificial animals (Qurbani) during Hajj and Eid, rather than warfare or execution. This act, paired with feeding the needy, symbolizes the dual dimensions of physical sacrifice and social generosity that earn divine pleasure. The hadith underscores the importance of tangible, bodily acts of worship in Shia piety, linking ritual obedience with charitable distribution.
